source.title: Label Noise Types and Their Effects on Deep Learning

record.file_problem: The supplied text is a full paper; some figure contents are represented only by captions and descriptions.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests several label-noise types and reports that, for uniform noise, training accuracy declines as the corruption rate rises and does not remain perfect. Its tested corruption rates stop at 75%.
record.gate_note: The paper cites the original memorization studies but does not reproduce complete random labeling, shuffled or noise inputs, dropout effects on random-label fitting, or learning order. Its own experiments use synthetic label noise at rates from 5% to 75%. The CIFAR100 plot has no extractable exact values in the supplied text.
record.test_reason: The study directly measures training and clean-test accuracy as uniform random label corruption increases. Its reported training accuracies contradict V4's perfect-fitting component under the tested training procedure. Complete random labeling is not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors emphasize that noise types produce different learning and generalization behavior, that feature-dependent noise can conceal damage when only noisy training and validation sets are monitored, and that noise-robust algorithms must be evaluated across noise types.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares synthetic uniform, structured class-dependent, locally concentrated, and feature-dependent label noise. It does not reproduce complete random labeling from the original studies; uniform noise is tested only up to 75% corruption.
record.method_sensitivity: Noise type and noise ratio change the reported training, validation, and test accuracies; dropout effects also vary by noise type, but are not a test of random-label fitting.

fits_no_version.finding: Dropout improves clean-test accuracy under partially corrupted labels, with improvements depending on noise type.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dropout's benefit for generalization under label noise depends on the noise distribution.

fits_no_version.finding: Feature-dependent noise can preserve apparently favorable training and noisy-validation behavior while substantially reducing clean-test accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training and noisy-validation performance can conceal generalization damage from feature-dependent label noise.

record.problems: Uniform-noise experiments do not reach 100% corruption. The supplied text gives exact uniform-noise accuracy values only for MNIST-Fashion; CIFAR100 results are plotted without extractable numbers. No uncertainty estimates are stated.
record.rows_left_out: CIFAR100 Figure 3 results are not entered because the supplied text provides no exact values for the plotted training, validation, and test accuracies. Other noise types are not entered because the versions concern randomly corrupted labels and the paper's results for those types do not establish that version-specific behavior.

untested.parts: Completely random training labels, chance test performance, and fitting under unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Training-time comparisons between true and random labels and convergence slowdown across random corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Zero corruption and corruption above 75%, including complete corruption and its chance-level endpoint; temporal separation of signal learning and noise memorization.
Random-label fitting with and without explicit regularization, and clean-label generalization after removing regularization.
Whether shared real-data patterns are learned before noisy labels; no separate clean/noisy learning trajectories are reported in the supplied text.

missing.what: The authors report repeating all Fashion-MNIST experiments with a three-layer MLP and obtaining results consistent with the CNN. This qualitative architecture comparison is missing; exact accuracies are unavailable.

record.verdict_notes: All recorded Table II values are transcribed correctly. The study is not an original source for these versions. Synthetic corruption supplies the labels whose spontaneous memorization is being measured; it does not exclude this experiment as deliberately induced behavior. Figure-only CIFAR100 results are already declared in rows_left_out. The reported training results establish failure to fit under this procedure, not an architectural inability to memorize.

versions.untested_parts: Complete random labeling and zero or near-zero training error under unchanged settings.
Small-constant-factor training time for random labels and convergence slowdown as random-label corruption rises.
Shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Corruption rates above 75%, including all labels corrupted; the study does not test whether training remains perfect while test error approaches chance.
Whether regularization prevents random-label fitting or its removal harms generalization on true labels.
Whether real patterns are learned before noisy or random labels.
